easy.def: A room where scientists work.
examples: The scientist is in the lab.
We visited a lab.
The lab has tools.

more.def: A room or building where scientists do experiments.
examples: The scientist mixed chemicals in the lab.
Our class visited a science lab.
The lab has microscopes and tubes.

easy.def: A small piece of paper that tells what something is.
examples: The label says milk.
I put a label on the box.
The label has my name.

more.def: A small piece of paper or cloth fixed to something to tell what it is.
examples: The label on the can says tomato soup.
I put a label on my lunch box.
The label inside the shirt shows the size.

easy.def: To stick a name on something.
examples: I label my box.
She labeled the jars.
Label the drawer.

more.def: To attach a small tag or sticker that tells people what something is.
examples: I labeled my lunch box with my name.
She labeled the jars of jam.
The teacher labeled the shelves.

easy.def: Hard work.
examples: The job took a lot of labor.
The labor was tiring.
Farm labor is hard.

more.def: Work, especially hard physical work.
examples: Building the house took a lot of labor.
Farm labor starts at dawn.
The workers' labor was done by sunset.

easy.def: A room where scientists do experiments.
examples: The scientist works in a laboratory.
The laboratory has tools.
We toured the laboratory.

more.def: A room or building with equipment where scientists do tests and experiments.
examples: The scientist worked in a laboratory.
The laboratory had microscopes and test tubes.
We toured a science laboratory.

easy.def: A string used to tie a shoe.
examples: I tie my laces.
The lace is untied.
My shoe lace broke.

more.def: A cord that is pulled through holes to fasten a shoe or boot.
examples: I tied my shoe laces.
The lace on my boot broke.
She pulled the laces tight.

easy.def: A fine, see-through cloth with patterns.
examples: The dress has lace.
The lace is white.
Grandma made lace.

more.def: A delicate cloth made from fine threads in open patterns.
examples: The wedding dress was trimmed with lace.
A lace curtain hung in the window.
Grandma made a lace collar.

easy.def: Not having enough of something.
examples: A lack of rain hurt the plants.
The lack of light made it hard to read.
A lack of sleep made him tired.

more.def: A condition of not having enough of something.
examples: A lack of rain made the garden dry.
The lack of snow meant we could not go sledding.
A lack of sleep makes it hard to learn.

easy.def: To not have enough of something.
examples: The plants lack water.
The soup lacks salt.
We lack a goalie.

more.def: To be without something, or not to have enough of it.
examples: The broth lacks flavor.
Our team lacks a good goalie this year.
Some desert plants lack leaves and have spines instead.

easy.def: A boy.
examples: The lad ran home.
A young lad helped us.
The lads played ball.

more.def: A boy or young man.
examples: The lad carried the basket to the market.
A young lad sold newspapers on the corner.
The lads in the story went fishing.

easy.def: Steps that you climb, made with two long sides.
examples: I climb the ladder.
The ladder is tall.
Dad put up the ladder.

more.def: A set of steps between two long sides that you climb up or down.
examples: I climbed the ladder to the roof.
Dad leaned the ladder against the wall.
The firefighter climbed a long ladder.

easy.def: A polite word for a woman.
examples: The lady smiled.
A kind lady helped me.
That lady has a hat.

more.def: A polite word for a woman, especially a grown-up.
examples: The lady at the bakery gave us each a free cookie.
An old lady held the door for the children.
Ladies and gentlemen, the show is about to begin.

easy.def: A place where a wild animal lives or hides.
examples: The bear's lair is in a cave.
A fox has a lair.
The wolf went to its lair.

more.def: A hidden home of a wild animal, such as a den or a cave.
examples: The bear's lair was a cave in the mountain.
A fox hid in its lair under the tree roots.
The dragon's lair was full of gold, in the story.

easy.def: A big body of water with land around it.
examples: We swim in the lake.
The lake is blue.
Ducks live on the lake.

more.def: A large body of fresh water with land all around it.
examples: We swam in the cool lake.
Ducks paddled across the lake.
The lake froze over in winter.

easy.def: A young sheep.
examples: The lamb is white.
The lamb ran.
The lamb stays near its mother.

more.def: A baby sheep.
examples: The lamb stayed close to its mother.
Spring is when lambs are born.
The little lamb skipped across the field.

easy.def: Not able to walk well because of an injury.
examples: The horse is lame.
The lame dog limped.
A lame cat sat by the road.

more.def: Not able to walk properly because of an injured leg or foot.
examples: The horse was lame and could not run.
The lame dog limped across the yard.
The vet treated the lame sheep.

easy.def: A light that you can switch on.
examples: Turn on the lamp.
The lamp is on my desk.
I read by a lamp.

more.def: A device that gives light, often with a shade, that you turn on and off.
examples: I turned on the lamp to read.
A lamp stood beside the bed.
The old lamp had a green shade.

easy.def: A long pole with a sharp point that a knight carried.
examples: The knight held a lance.
The lance is long.
He carried a lance.

more.def: A long, pointed pole that a knight carried when riding a horse.
examples: The knight held his lance high.
A long lance leaned against the castle wall.
In the story, the knight rode with a lance and a shield.

easy.def: The dry part of the Earth.
examples: The ship reached land.
Frogs live on land and in water.
The land is flat here.

more.def: The solid part of the Earth's surface that is not covered by water.
examples: After days at sea, the sailors saw land.
Farmers plant crops on good land.
Turtles lay their eggs on land.

easy.def: To come down from the air.
examples: The plane will land.
The bird landed.
A bee landed on my hand.

more.def: To come down to the ground or water after flying.
examples: The plane landed safely at the airport.
A butterfly landed on my finger.
The geese landed on the lake.

easy.def: The place where you get off a boat or plane.
examples: We saw the plane's landing.
The landing was smooth.
The boat made a landing.

more.def: The act of coming down to the ground or onto the water, or the place where this happens.
examples: The pilot made a smooth landing.
The boats pulled up to the landing.
We watched the rocket's landing on TV.

easy.def: The flat part at the top or middle of stairs.
examples: I waited on the landing.
The cat slept on the landing.
There is a window on the landing.

more.def: A flat area at the top of a set of stairs or between two sets of stairs.
examples: I waited on the landing at the top of the stairs.
Family photos hung on the wall of the landing.
A window brightens the landing.

easy.def: A person who owns a building and rents it out.
examples: The landlord fixed the sink.
Our landlord is kind.
We pay rent to the landlord.

more.def: A person who owns a house or building and lets others pay to live in it.
examples: The landlord fixed the leaky sink.
We pay our rent to the landlord each month.
Our landlord painted the walls.

related.def: A person whose job is to plan and care for gardens.

easy.def: Everything you can see when you look out over the land.
examples: The landscape was green.
We looked at the mountain landscape.
She painted a landscape.

more.def: A wide view of land, with hills, fields, trees and sky, or a picture that shows it.
examples: From the top of the hill, we saw a landscape of farms and forests.
The painter loved to paint a landscape with a river and mountains.
Snow changed the whole landscape into a white world.

easy.def: To make a yard or garden look nice.
examples: We landscape the yard.
Dad landscaped the garden.
They landscaped the park.

more.def: To change the way a piece of land looks by adding plants, paths or rocks.
examples: We landscaped the front yard with new flowers and a stone path.
Workers landscaped the park by planting trees around the pond.
They landscaped the hillside with grass and bushes.

easy.def: A narrow road.
examples: We walked down the lane.
A country lane.
The lane is quiet.

more.def: A narrow road or path.
examples: We walked down a quiet country lane.
A dirt lane led to the farm.
The lane was lined with trees.

easy.def: A strip for one line of cars or swimmers.
examples: Stay in your lane.
The pool has six lanes.
The road has two lanes.

more.def: A strip of road, track or pool for one line of cars, runners or swimmers.
examples: Stay in your lane when you swim.
The highway has three lanes.
Each runner had a lane on the track.

easy.def: The words people use to talk and write.
examples: Spanish is a language.
Babies learn language by listening.
Sign language uses your hands.

more.def: A system of words that people use to speak, write, and understand each other.
examples: She can speak three languages: English, French, and Arabic.
People who cannot hear may use sign language.
He is learning a new language before his trip.

easy.def: A light you can carry, inside a case.
examples: We lit a lantern.
The lantern glowed.
He carried a lantern at night.

more.def: A lamp inside a glass or paper case that you can carry or hang up.
examples: We hung a lantern from the tent pole so that we could see at night.
Colorful paper lanterns lit the garden for the festival.
He carried a lantern down the dark path.

easy.def: The top of your legs when you sit.
examples: The cat sat on my lap.
I held the book in my lap.
She put the baby on her lap.

more.def: The flat top of your thighs when you sit down.
examples: The cat curled up in my lap.
The little boy fell asleep in his grandpa's lap.
I held the book open in my lap.

easy.def: One time around a track.
examples: I ran one lap.
We swam ten laps.
The runners did three laps.

more.def: One complete trip around a track or pool.
examples: She ran four laps around the track.
The swimmers did ten laps in the pool.
He was in the lead on the last lap.

easy.def: A small computer you can carry.
examples: I use a laptop.
The laptop is on the table.
She has a laptop.

more.def: A small computer that folds shut and can be carried and used on your lap.
examples: I used a laptop to write my report.
The laptop fits in my backpack.
She closed her laptop.

easy.def: Big.
examples: A large dog.
The box is large.
A large cup of milk.

more.def: Big in size or amount.
examples: A large crowd gathered in the park.
The elephant is the largest land animal.
She ordered a large glass of milk.

easy.def: A baked food made of flat noodles layered with cheese and sauce.
examples: Mom made lasagna.
I like lasagna.
The lasagna had lots of cheese.

more.def: An Italian dish made of flat pasta sheets layered with cheese, sauce and sometimes meat.
examples: Mom baked a big pan of lasagna for dinner.
I like lasagna with lots of cheese and tomato sauce.
The lasagna was layered with spinach and cheese.

easy.def: A very thin, strong beam of light.
examples: The laser is red.
A laser points.
The teacher used a laser pointer.

more.def: A very narrow, strong beam of light that is used for cutting and many other jobs.
examples: The teacher used a laser pointer on the screen.
Doctors use a laser for some operations.
The laser beam shone across the room.

easy.def: One of the hairs that grow on the edge of your eyelid.
examples: I have a long lash.
My lash is long.
She has dark lashes.

more.def: One of the short hairs that grow along the edge of the eyelid.
examples: A lash fell in my eye.
She has long dark lashes.
I made a wish on a fallen eyelash.

easy.def: To tie something tightly.
examples: We lash the boat to the dock.
He lashed the boxes.
She lashed the sticks.

more.def: To tie something firmly with a rope or cord.
examples: We lashed the boat to the dock with a thick rope.
He lashed the boxes to the top of the car.
They lashed three logs together to make a raft.

easy.def: Coming after all the others.
examples: I was last in line.
This is the last page.
She ate the last grape.

more.def: Coming at the end, or most recent.
examples: The last bus leaves the station at midnight.
I saw my cousins last summer.
He ate the last slice of pizza on the plate.

easy.def: To go on for a time.
examples: The show lasts one hour.
The snow did not last.
Will the toy last?

more.def: To continue for a certain length of time, or to stay in good condition.
examples: The storm lasted all night, but the morning was calm.
These strong boots will last for years.
A summer day lasts longer than a winter day.

easy.def: Going on for a long time.
examples: They have a lasting friendship.
A lasting peace.
The painting had a lasting effect.

more.def: Continuing for a long time, or for always.
examples: The two girls formed a lasting friendship at camp.
The treaty brought a lasting peace.
The lesson had a lasting effect on him.

easy.def: A small bar that holds a door or gate shut.
examples: The gate has a latch.
Lift the latch.
The latch is stuck.

more.def: A small bar or catch that holds a door, a gate or a window closed.
examples: I lifted the latch and pushed open the garden gate.
The latch on the barn door was stuck.
Dad fixed the broken latch on the window.

easy.def: To shut a door or gate with a small bar.
examples: Latch the gate.
He latched the door.
She latched the window.

more.def: To close a door, gate or window with a small bar or catch.
examples: Please latch the gate so the dog cannot get out.
He latched the barn door for the night.
She latched the window against the wind.

easy.def: After the right time.
examples: I am late.
The bus is late.
It is late at night.

more.def: Coming after the expected time, or near the end of a period of time.
examples: The train was late because of the snow.
We stayed up late on New Year's Eve.
The leaves fall in late autumn.

easy.def: After the right time.
examples: She woke up late.
We ate late.
He got to school late.

more.def: After the usual or expected time.
examples: I woke up late, so I missed the bus.
The movie ended late, and we got home after dark.
She arrived late and tiptoed to her seat.

easy.def: Not long ago.
examples: I have been tired lately.
We have not seen him lately.
It has been warm lately.

more.def: Recently, in the past few days or weeks.
examples: I have been very tired lately.
We have not seen our neighbor lately.
Have you read any good books lately?

easy.def: After this time.
examples: See you later.
I will eat later.
She came later.

more.def: At a time after now, or after another time that was named.
examples: I will do my homework later, after we play outside.
The rain stopped, and the sun came out an hour later.
We can talk about it later.

easy.def: To make happy sounds because something is funny.
examples: I laugh at funny jokes.
The baby laughed.
We laughed at the clown.

more.def: To make sounds with your voice that show you think something is funny or you are happy.
examples: The whole class laughed at the silly story.
She laughed so hard that her stomach hurt.
Dad laughs whenever the dog chases its tail.

easy.def: The sound you make when something is funny.
examples: She has a loud laugh.
We had a good laugh.
I heard his laugh in the next room.

more.def: The happy sound a person makes when something is funny.
examples: Her laugh is so loud that you can hear it across the playground.
The joke got a big laugh from everyone.
We had a good laugh about the mix-up.

easy.def: The sound of people laughing.
examples: I heard laughter from the playground.
The joke filled the room with laughter.
Laughter is a happy sound.

more.def: The sound or act of laughing.
examples: The room filled with laughter when the clown came in.
Their laughter could be heard down the hall.
The funny movie brought tears of laughter.

easy.def: To send something up or out into the air or water.
examples: They will launch the rocket.
We launched a boat.
He launched the kite.

more.def: To send something such as a rocket or boat out with force, or to start something new.
examples: The scientists launched a rocket into space.
The crew launched the boat from the shore.
The school will launch a new reading club this fall.

easy.def: The sending of a rocket or boat.
examples: We watched the launch on TV.
The launch was loud.
The boat launch was fun.

more.def: The act of sending a rocket, ship or something new out into the world.
examples: The whole class watched the launch of the space shuttle.
A boat launch let us slide our canoe into the water.
The launch of the new book was a big event.

easy.def: Clothes that need washing, or have just been washed.
examples: Mom does the laundry.
The laundry is in the basket.
I folded the laundry.

more.def: Clothes and sheets that are being washed or have just been washed.
examples: Mom did the laundry on Saturday.
The clean laundry was folded in a basket.
He put the dirty laundry in the machine.

easy.def: Hot, melted rock that comes out of a volcano.
examples: Lava flows from the volcano.
The lava is hot.
The lava is red.

more.def: Hot, melted rock that pours out of a volcano and then cools into hard rock.
examples: Red lava flowed down the side of the volcano.
Lava is so hot that it can burn trees.
The cooled lava turned into black rock.

easy.def: A rule that everyone in a place must follow.
examples: It is a law to wear a seat belt.
The town made a new law.
Every country has laws.

more.def: A rule made by the government that people must obey.
examples: There is a law that cars must stop for school buses.
The mayor signed a new law about recycling.
Laws help keep people safe.

easy.def: The grass in front of or behind a house.
examples: Dad mows the lawn.
The lawn is green.
I play on the lawn.

more.def: An area of short, cut grass near a house or in a park.
examples: Dad mows the lawn every Saturday.
Children played on the lawn.
The sprinkler watered the front lawn.

easy.def: A case in court.
examples: The company had a lawsuit.
The lawsuit was long.
He filed a lawsuit.

more.def: A case that is brought to a court of law when one person says another has wronged them.
examples: The company faced a lawsuit.
The lawsuit lasted two years.
She filed a lawsuit against the store.

easy.def: A person with a job helping people with the law.
examples: The lawyer works in court.
My aunt is a lawyer.
A lawyer reads many laws.

more.def: A person whose job is to give advice about laws and speak for people in court.
examples: My aunt is a lawyer who helps families.
The lawyer spoke to the judge.
Lawyers study the law for many years.

easy.def: To put something down gently.
examples: Lay the book on the table.
Mom laid the baby in the crib.
Lay your coat here.

more.def: To put something down in a flat or careful way.
examples: Lay the cards face down on the table.
She laid the baby in the crib.
Workers laid bricks in a neat row.

easy.def: To make an egg.
examples: Hens lay eggs.
The hen laid an egg.
Birds lay eggs in nests.

more.def: To produce an egg from the body.
examples: Chickens lay eggs almost every day.
The turtle crawled up the beach to lay her eggs.
Robins lay blue eggs in the spring.

easy.def: One flat piece over another.
examples: The cake has three layers.
A layer of snow.
Put on a layer of paint.

more.def: A flat thickness of something that covers a surface or lies between other things.
examples: The cake had three layers.
A layer of snow covered the road.
I wore a sweater as a second layer.

easy.def: The way things are set out on a page or in a place.
examples: I like the layout of the page.
The layout of the room is nice.
We changed the layout.

more.def: The way that parts of something are arranged on a page, a map or in a room.
examples: The layout of the room made it easy to move around.
I drew the layout of my dream bedroom.
The book has a clear layout, with pictures next to the words.

easy.def: Not wanting to work or move.
examples: The lazy cat slept all day.
I feel lazy on hot days.
A lazy dog lay in the sun.

more.def: Not willing to work or use energy.
examples: He felt too lazy to get up and close the door.
We spent a lazy afternoon reading by the pool.
He was too lazy to put his dishes in the sink.
